meta.scope: Guyana batch 2 — Oil production depth (FPSOs), NRF flows, non-oil GDP, fiscal/budget, inflation, external accounts, Local Content, and cash-transfer social spending. Continues the oil-transformation picture.

candidates.title: FPSO fleet (Liza Destiny, Liza Unity, Prosperity, ONE Guyana)
candidates.description: Floating Production, Storage and Offloading vessels that constitute current production capacity. Four vessels online; further FPSOs (Uaru/Errea Wittu and beyond) scheduled to push capacity toward 1.3 mbd.
candidates.notes: Physical production platform. Each successive FPSO has driven step-changes in output and in NRF inflows. Continuously cited in production and revenue tracking.

candidates.title: NRF inflows and withdrawals
candidates.publisher: Bank of Guyana / Ministry of Finance
candidates.description: Periodic reporting of deposits into and withdrawals from the Natural Resource Fund (profit oil, royalties, signature bonuses; approved budget transfers).
candidates.notes: Operational fiscal pulse of the oil era. Cumulative deposits multi-billion USD; withdrawals finance a large and rising share of the national budget. Balance tracked in the low-to-mid single-digit billions of USD.

candidates.title: Non-oil GDP
candidates.publisher: Bureau of Statistics / Bank of Guyana
candidates.description: GDP excluding crude-oil extraction. Grows more moderately than headline GDP but is itself stimulated by oil-financed public investment and local-content activity.
candidates.notes: Key analytical distinction. Non-oil growth in the high-single to low-double digits is frequently cited as evidence of spillovers; critics note that much of it is still oil-money circulating through construction and public services.

candidates.title: National Budget
candidates.description: Annual national budget. Increasingly financed by NRF withdrawals; supports large public investment, cash transfers, wages and social programmes.
candidates.notes: Operational spending framework of the boom. NRF transfers now cover a material share (order of 30%+) of a rapidly expanding budget.

candidates.title: Consumer Price Index / Inflation
candidates.publisher: Bureau of Statistics / Bank of Guyana
candidates.description: Urban consumer price index and inflation measures. Inflation has remained relatively contained compared with regional peers, with food prices the main driver.
candidates.notes: Price-stability node. Average inflation in the low-to-mid single digits in recent years; food inflation higher and more relevant for poorer households.

candidates.title: Balance of Payments / External accounts
candidates.description: Balance of payments and external-sector statistics. Large current-account surpluses driven by oil exports; capital account reflects FPSO and related investment imports.
candidates.notes: External counterpart of the oil boom. Current-account surplus remains large even as import bills for FPSOs and investment goods spike in delivery years.

candidates.title: Local Content Act / local-content regime
candidates.description: Legal and regulatory framework requiring and monitoring local participation in the oil and gas value chain. Intended channel for non-oil employment and enterprise development.
candidates.notes: Spillover-policy node. Continuously cited as the main institutional attempt to convert oil activity into broader domestic employment and firm growth.

candidates.title: Cash transfers and social grants
candidates.description: Expanding set of cash grants, vouchers and social transfers financed in part by NRF withdrawals. Visible instrument of oil-revenue redistribution.
candidates.notes: Lived redistribution node. Budget documents and independent commentary track the growth of cash grants and related transfers as a primary way households feel the oil boom.

candidates.title: Public debt
candidates.publisher: Ministry of Finance / Bank of Guyana
candidates.description: Stock of public debt relative to GDP. Remains moderate by regional standards despite rapid spending growth, supported by oil-revenue inflows.
candidates.notes: Sustainability indicator. Debt-to-GDP has risen modestly with domestic issuance but stays well below levels typical of stressed regional peers.

candidates.title: CARICOM membership
candidates.description: Membership of the Caribbean Community. Primary regional-integration framework for trade, movement and political coordination.
candidates.notes: Core regional-architecture node. Continuously cited as Guyana’s principal formal integration framework in the Caribbean.

proposed_edges.basis: The FPSO fleet is the physical production platform for current oil output.
Inflows and withdrawals are the operational flows of the Natural Resource Fund.
Approved NRF withdrawals are a major financing source of the national budget.
Non-oil GDP is the residual of total GDP after excluding oil extraction.
Local-content rules are designed to link oil activity to domestic employment and enterprise.
Cash grants and social transfers are increasingly financed by NRF withdrawals.
Balance of payments is compiled by the Bank of Guyana.
CARICOM membership structures a portion of regional trade and services flows.
